title: The hackathon
narration:
I'm building a project called CounterPilot for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon. If you haven't heard of a hackathon, think of it as a building challenge: take an idea and turn it into something that actually works.

This one brings developers together online from around the world, with ten days to build using Meta's AI models and a million dollars in total prizes. One of the themes is 'Build for Your World.' My project focuses on something practical: helping make sense of automotive parts requests.
record: Show the official event title, then its Build for Your World theme. Cut to the CounterPilot homepage. The million dollars is the total prize pool.
overlay: CounterPilot | Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon

title: One request, three parts
narration:
'I need brakes, an air filter, and a belt.' That sounds simple. But which brakes? Which belt? And what vehicle are they going on?

Those little details turn one sentence into a conversation. I wanted to explore whether AI could help organize that conversation without guessing at the important information.
record: Hold on the empty chat. Overlay: One request. Three different parts.

title: Make the request
narration:
Here's the request: 'I need brakes, an air filter, and a belt for my 2019 Toyota RAV4.'

CounterPilot keeps that as three separate items. They share the vehicle information, but each part has its own questions. The air filter can already have a catalog record available while the brakes and belt still need clarification.
record: Type and send: I need brakes, an air filter, and a belt for my 2019 Toyota RAV4. Show the three-item checklist, available air-filter card and brake question.

title: Clarify each item
narration:
For the brakes, I'll choose brake pads, then front. That answer belongs to the brakes—it shouldn't change the other items.

Next, I'll specify a serpentine belt. Now the conversation can show records for all three items together. It remembers the original request while we work through the missing details.
record: Choose Brake pads, then front, then Serpentine belt. Use the checklist to jump between all three cards.

title: What the AI does
narration:
The AI helps understand what I'm asking for. The catalog supplies the actual records. I don't want a convincing answer with an invented part number.

These are demonstration records with simulated fitment, and they're labeled that way. This is a working prototype of the conversation and lookup process—not something to use for purchasing or installing parts yet.
record: Open Source and restrictions on a card. Hold on the demo label, part number and source information. Keep the disclosures readable.

title: Correct one item
narration:
And if I change my mind, I shouldn't have to start over. Here, I'll change the air filter to a cabin filter.

That updates one item while keeping the brakes and belt. Getting those everyday corrections right is a big part of making this feel useful.
record: Send: Change the air filter to a cabin filter. Show the changed filter and preserved brake and belt items.
overlay: Change one item. Keep the rest.

title: Save useful results
narration:
After the lookup, CounterPilot offers to save the displayed results to Garage. I can save one card or all the displayed records, then come back to them grouped under the vehicle.

And if I need something else, I can add another part without rebuilding the whole request.
record: Save all displayed records, open Garage and show the three records grouped under the RAV4. Close Garage, click Add another part and leave the prepared message unsent.
overlay: Save the displayed records to Garage

title: Ask viewers
narration:
That's what I'm building for the hackathon: a practical way to turn an everyday request into an organized conversation, with clear questions and traceable results.

There's still more work ahead, especially around verified catalog data. If you've worked a parts counter—or struggled to explain what your car needs—what would you want this to handle? I'd love to hear your examples.
record: Return to the grouped results. End on CounterPilot — What should it handle next?
overlay: CounterPilot — What should it handle next?
